review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas and has no loops or competing rules, so the findings are about missing simp interface. I read quotientTransition_map_id and the uses of `π_map` in QuotientTransitions, OpenNormalDiagram, CompactDiscreteTorsion and Mathlib's ContCohomology/Functoriality. I did not check the downstream effect of adding simp attributes, and I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed simp forms fire or whether `quotientTransition_map_id` interacts with other simp lemmas. The second finding (the `π_map` pattern) is the weaker of the two, since the pattern appears in other files but I did not count every occurrence.

findings.problem: `quotientTransition_map_id` (QuotientTransitions.lean, line 155) is the canonical identification of the self-transition map with `𝟙`, but it has no `@[simp]` attribute. The sibling lemmas `quotientTransitionHom_mk` and `quotientTransitionIncl_val` are simp. So `map (quotientTransitionHom N N _) (quotientTransitionIncl X _) n` does not normalise to `𝟙 _` under `simp`. Each use needs a manual `rw`, as here and in OpenNormalDiagram.lean line 317. The proof argument `le_refl N` is a proposition, so a simp lemma would also match other proofs of `N ≤ N`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `quotientTransition_map_id` with `@[simp]` in QuotientTransitions.lean. Optionally also add a simp lemma `(map (quotientTransitionHom N N h) (quotientTransitionIncl X h) n).hom a = a`, stated for arbitrary `h : N ≤ N`. The zero case can then be `simp [hzM]` instead of `rw` followed by `simp only`.
findings.benefit: The identity transition normalises automatically wherever `N ≤ N` arises, for example after `refine ⟨M, le_refl M, ?_⟩`. Callers no longer need to name the lemma and fix its arguments for `rw`. The left side is a specific term that rewrites to `𝟙`, so there is no loop risk.

findings.problem: Mathlib's continuous-cohomology `π_map` is `@[reassoc]` only, with no `elementwise` form. The analogous group-cohomology `π_map` is `@[reassoc, elementwise]`. So every elementwise use needs a hand-written `congrArg (fun f => f.hom z)` followed by `simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply] using h.symm`. This file does it in the degree-zero lemma (lines 119–126) and again for the successor case (about lines 165–175, plus the final `h` near the end). CompactDiscreteTorsion.lean has the same pattern near line 94. The same happens for `cyclesMap_i`, `toCycles_i` and the `cochainsMap` `comm` lemmas. Note that `(π X n).hom (cocyclesMap ... ).hom z` and `(map ...).hom ((π ...).hom z)` are the two canonical sides, but no lemma states them, so there is no normal form that `simp` can reach.
findings.proposed_change: Add a project-level lemma stating `π_map` pointwise. For example: `(map φ f n).hom ((π X n).hom z) = (π Y n).hom ((cocyclesMap φ f n).hom z)`, proved from `π_map` with `ConcreteCategory.comp_apply`. Orient it consistently (cocycle-map side into cohomology, or the reverse) and decide whether it is `@[simp]`. Use it in `hπG` as `rw [← π_map_apply]`, or `simpa using`, in place of the `congrArg`/`calc` blocks. If the project is not already using Mathlib's `elementwise` attribute, this lemma could be generated with `elementwise` on a local re-statement.
findings.benefit: This removes several 8–10 line `congrArg`/`calc`/`simpa only` blocks in this file and in CompactDiscreteTorsion.lean. It also gives `simp` and `rw` a predictable normal form for elements of `continuousCohomology` that come from cocycles.
